clue.text: Fit woman takes exercise

explanation.surface: A healthy woman keeps up her workouts.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to make it suitable, to fit it to a purpose.

clue.text: A British eccentric resident in Australia?

parts.note: an original is an eccentric person

explanation.surface: An odd Briton who has settled down under.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the answer means a native Australian, not any resident.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aboriginal person is one of the original inhabitants of Australia.

clue.text: Fool of a girl going topless

indicators.note: the word for girl loses its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: A silly young woman sunbathing without her bikini top.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a foolish person, a donkey in the figurative sense.

clue.text: One changing in tent for a laugh

indicators.note: one letter of the tent word is changed for another

parts.note: a teepee is a conical tent

explanation.surface: Someone getting dressed inside a tent just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: In TEEPEE the P becomes H.
explanation.definitionFit: Tee-hee is a giggle, a sound made in laughter.

clue.text: One who's up close?

parts.note: someone right next to an event, standing by it while it happens, is close to it without taking part

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone who gets a close look at things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up close' suggests intimacy; the clue means simply someone present and standing near a happening.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker is present at an event, close to it, but not involved in it.

clue.text: Butterfly is absolutely filled with colour

parts.note: a vessel that brims is full to the top
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A butterfly so vivid it seems saturated with colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The brimstone is a yellow butterfly common in Europe.

clue.text: Power of decision thus involves affirmations

indicators.note: involves means the word for thus wraps round the other piece

parts.note: ays, a variant spelling of ayes, are yes votes

explanation.surface: Authority to decide comes from people saying yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the say-so means having the authority to decide.

clue.text: Condition after pirate's drunk alcohol before meal

indicators.note: after puts the condition word behind the jumble
a drunk is mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A drunken pirate on the hard stuff before his dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken to stimulate appetite before a meal.

clue.text: Toy with menu card being reproduced on paper?

indicators.note: reproduced suggests copying, here the letters are made again in a new order

explanation.surface: Fiddling with a restaurant menu that is being photocopied.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: documentary evidence is evidence on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Documentary means consisting of written documents, as in documentary records.

clue.text: Government way in France is to imprison Left

indicators.note: to imprison means the street word holds the other piece inside

explanation.surface: French authorities lock up a left-wing activist.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule means government, as in a period of direct rule.

clue.text: Bad language upsetting nicest boy?

indicators.note: upsetting the letters knocks them over into a new order

explanation.surface: Swearing that would shock the best-behaved little lad.
explanation.definitionFit: An obscenity is an indecent word, the kind that counts as foul language.

clue.text: Top forty — ancient, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us to speak those numeral letters out loud

parts.note: forty written in the ancient Roman numerals is XL

explanation.surface: Something about an old chart of the forty best records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top forty' looks like a pop chart; 'Top' alone is the verb, and the two letters for forty, spoken, give the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To top a rival is to outdo or surpass them, a verb sense matching the answer.

clue.text: Art school for which number of books printed is millions

parts.note: an impression is the set of copies of a book printed in one run

explanation.surface: A movement in painting whose print run reached millions.
explanation.walkthrough: In publishing, an impression is all the copies printed at one time.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressionism is the nineteenth-century French movement in painting, a school of art.

clue.text: Royal — not English — one friendly, in the main

indicators.note: not means the letter for English is dropped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A royal who isn't English, yet chummy, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not English' strips E from PRINCE, leaving PRINC.
explanation.definitionFit: Principally means mainly, chiefly, for the most part.

clue.text: Madman taking drink in carriage

indicators.note: taking means the madman word holds the drink word inside

parts.note: dement is an old word for a madman

explanation.surface: A lunatic having a drink inside a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' is not a vehicle but bearing or posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Deportment means the way a person carries themselves, their posture and bearing.

clue.text: Or this would be antelopes, sacred creature of Egypt

indicators.note: the clue says 'Or' with this answer in front would make the antelopes, so the answer is those antelopes with Or taken away

explanation.surface: A remark that some animal could pass for a herd of antelopes, plus a sacred Egyptian beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The oribi is a small antelope; put OR in front of the answer and you get its plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird was worshipped in ancient Egypt as sacred to the god Thoth.

clue.text: Prisoner needs knowledge to form moral sense

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
science in its old sense means knowledge

explanation.surface: A jailbird must learn things to develop a sense of right and wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscience is the inner sense of right and wrong that guides behaviour.

clue.text: Losing head, sought to turn and run away

indicators.note: losing head drops the first letter

parts.note: to addle or turn is to go bad, as eggs or milk do

explanation.surface: Someone beheaded wanted to spin round and flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is a lighthearted word for running away hurriedly.

clue.text: Local authority visit about heartless treatment of infant and youth

indicators.note: about means the visit word goes round the rest

parts.note: a call is a short visit

indicators.note: the words are treated heartlessly, losing everything but their first and last letters

explanation.surface: A council inspector checks on cruelty to a baby and a teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless treatment of' leaves IT from infant and YH from youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A city hall is the headquarters of a municipal government, the local authority.

clue.text: Inventor inconvenienced by Amish creed?

indicators.note: the letters are put out, disturbed from their order

explanation.surface: An inventor finds the beliefs of a plain-living sect a hindrance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek mathematician of Syracuse is famed for inventions such as his water screw.

clue.text: Puss rejected old dish

indicators.note: rejected means the word is turned back on itself

explanation.surface: The cat turned up its nose at a stale bowl of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a Mexican dish of a folded tortilla with a filling.

clue.text: Prepare for burial and disposal together?

definitions.meaning: to ... a corpse is to make it ready for the funeral
an arrangement, the way things are disposed together on a page or site

explanation.surface: Getting a body ready and putting the bits in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay out means prepare a body; a layout is an arrangement of parts.

clue.text: One may study the crazy hybrid calypso-shanty

indicators.note: a hybrid mixes things up, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone might analyse a strange musical cross of Caribbean song and sea song.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychoanalyst examines the minds of the mentally disturbed, in informal terms the crazy.

clue.text: Resort has left bad housing

parts.note: Hove is an English seaside resort next to Brighton

explanation.surface: A holiday town has abandoned its run-down homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovel is a squalid, wretched dwelling, poor housing.

clue.text: One of elevated leaders of regimes in Middle East?

definitions.text: One of elevated leaders of regimes in Middle East?

indicators.note: in a down entry elevated means the letters are raised, read upward
the leaders of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: One of the exalted rulers of Middle Eastern states.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince in the Middle East.

clue.text: Whisky associated with east side of Jura island

indicators.note: the east side of a word written left to right is its final letter

explanation.surface: A single malt from the Scottish island of Jura.
explanation.walkthrough: Jura is a Hebridean island famous for whisky, a decoy island.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is a Mediterranean island nation south of Sicily.

clue.text: Running aged movie for entertainment on screen

indicators.note: running here means the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Showing an old film to amuse people watching a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic games are played on a screen as a form of amusement.

clue.text: A marine inlet

parts.note: RM, Royal Marine, is a marine

explanation.surface: A small bay of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm of the sea is a narrow inlet.

clue.text: A shade sad after Diana, perhaps

indicators.note: after puts the sad word behind the Diana word

parts.note: Diana, Princess of Wales, was a royal

explanation.surface: A gloomy feeling following Princess Diana's death.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep, bright shade of blue colour.

clue.text: Risk provoking secretary with little time

parts.note: a temp is a temporary secretary

explanation.surface: A secretary who arrives briefly might cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt fate is to take the chance of provoking misfortune.
